one_line_contribution: A causal, action-mix-controlled measurement that a retrieved memory block imprints its action histogram onto a sequential agent's policy largely independently of the current state, plus MAC — a per-retrieval subtraction of that query-independent component — claimed to beat both scalar context scaling (CFG/CAD) and a fixed bank-wide base-rate offset.
closest_prior_work: Zhao et al. 2021 (Calibrate Before Use), and it threatens the proposal more than the proposal admits. CC's content-free probe is computed WITH the demonstrations in the prompt, i.e. p(y | 'N/A', demos): if the demonstration block changes per query, CC's estimate changes per query automatically. MAC, as described in E2/E3 (content-free goal + templated observation + the same injected block), is literally CC recomputed per retrieval. The claim in Related Work that 'no prior calibration paper has had to answer whether adaptivity buys anything' is therefore backwards — CC was always per-context; the static-demonstration setting merely made the per-context estimate constant. The 'global bank base-rate offset' that P4 is defined against is not 'what classic ICL calibration reduces to'; it is a weaker estimator the calibration literature never proposed. Generative Calibration (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023 Findings), which estimates the label marginal by Monte-Carlo sampling under the actual prompt, and Batch Calibration (Zhou et al. 2023), which estimates the shift from the actual inputs, are both per-context estimators as well. On the decoding side, PMI/surface-form-competition scoring (Holtzman et al. 2021) and noisy-channel prompting (Min et al. 2022) are the same instrument — divide out the action's unconditional propensity under the context. What survives as genuinely new is the sequential-agent transfer plus the E1-E3 measurement, not the estimator and not the adaptivity.
strongest_objection: P4 — explicitly named as 'the second confirmatory test and the novelty-bearing one' — is a comparison against a strawman. Beating a fixed bank-wide log-marginal offset by 4 points does not establish that per-retrieval calibration is a new contribution; it establishes that a per-query estimator beats an estimator nobody proposed, while the literal 2021 method (CC with the current block in the probe prompt) IS MAC. If P4 wins, the paper's own pre-commitment ('classic contextual calibration transfers unchanged to agent memory') is the honest headline whether P4 wins or loses, which means the headline test cannot discriminate. Second, and nearly as damaging: the Short Hypothesis asserts imprinting is 'the dominant source of memory-induced breakage', but no experiment tests dominance. All four E1 arms (LOW/MID/HIGH/IRR-HIGH) are matched within 5% on token count, deliberately holding constant the one lever the pilot actually proved causal (k=7 to k=3 eliminated the harm from the same bank). There is no share x volume factorial anywhere, and the k=2 arm — the pilot's own validated neutraliser — enters E5 only conditionally, on a 500-game subset whose MDE (~4.2 pts) equals the effect size MAC is predicted to produce. So the plan can show that action share has an effect while leaving 'imprinting rather than volume explains the pilot harm' entirely untested. Third, IRR-HIGH is a weak boundary control in ALFWorld: bottom-decile-retrieval items are still ALFWorld trajectories with the same verb vocabulary ('go to', 'take', 'open'), so 'topically irrelevant' and 'action-mix matched' are nearly collinear and P1's <25%/>=50% thresholds may be unfalsifiable in practice.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Drop the strawman framing: put literal per-query Contextual Calibration in as the named baseline, concede MAC = CC-per-retrieval, and make the contribution the measurement (E1-E3 factorisation R², drift, stratified fix/break) plus the head-to-head against CFG and against the zero-forward-pass literal-histogram estimator of ablation (e). If the free histogram estimator ties the probe — a live possibility given E0 already computes the block histogram — there is no method left and the paper should be planned as a measurement paper from the start. (2) Add a share x injection-volume factorial in E1 (2 shares x 2 k values, token count varied not fixed) and put k=2 in the full 1,000-game confirmatory grid, so the 'dominant source' claim becomes testable rather than assumed. (3) Fix the tuning asymmetry: the claim that sweeping gamma over 5 values against lambda's 3 'favours the competitor' is backwards — selection on a 200-game split (MDE ~6-7 pts) is mostly selecting noise, and more grid points means more winner's-curse and worse held-out transfer for CFG. Use the same grid size for both, or select via the E6 null distribution. (4) P5 is currently untestable as written: instruction debiasing, action-balanced retrieval and GEPA-selected demonstrations are never all run on the 1,000-game held-out set (only the screening winner is, and GEPA only appears single-turn). Either carry all three into E5 or restate P5 at the power it actually has. (5) E8/P8 rests on three GEPA runs, one per condition, with no seed replication — the track's own pilot showed a null replicate reproducing the best treatment's apparent gain; run >=3 seeds per condition or drop the quantitative >=2.5-point claim. (6) Resolve the internal contradiction between Risk 11 (probe cost 'amortised across steps using that block') and E0/P4 (the block drifts step to step): if adaptivity is necessary, amortisation is not available, and the cost table must include one extra forward pass per decision step. (7) Run the pre-committed searches before, not after, writing the novelty claim.
missing_baseline: Volume reduction (k=2) at full power in the confirmatory grid. It is the pilot's own validated neutraliser and the direct rival explanation for the harm MAC claims to remove, yet E5 admits it only as a conditional sixth condition on 500 games if it happens to win screening. A reviewer will demand MAC vs k=2 at n=1,000 paired, because 'MAC produces gain where k=2 only removes harm' is a claim the plan asserts (Baselines item 6) without powering. Secondary omissions: MAC+CFG combined (needed to show the channels are complementary rather than substitutable, which is what the factorisation claim actually implies), and a plain PMI-style baseline that divides by p(a | block) with no content-free template at all, which would price the entire probe apparatus against a one-line scoring change.
preprint_collision: The check is a declared null: zero searches returned results, for the second consecutive round, on a tooling failure. The proposal is commendably honest about this and refuses to read silence as novelty — but under the standard applied here that leaves novelty unestablished rather than neutral, and it is a weakness, not a wash. The three risks it flags (frequency/majority bias in LLM function-calling; calibrated or contrastive decoding on agentic memory; retrieval-induced action drift in memory-augmented agents) are exactly the low-hanging 2025-2026 extensions of Calibrate Before Use, and I share the proposal's own assessment that at least one probably exists; I cannot verify which, having not searched. What can be said from indexed work alone is that the adaptivity premise is already weakened: CC's probe is per-context by construction, and Generative Calibration and Batch Calibration both estimate the shift from the live prompt/inputs, so 'per-retrieval estimation is an open question classic calibration could not pose' does not survive contact with 2021-2023 papers, let alone 2026 preprints. Note also that the proposal's own fallback (c) — 'if a preprint already establishes per-retrieval calibration under RAG-style variable demonstrations, the novelty claim collapses to the agentic/sequential transfer' — is already the accurate description of the submission as written.
